phenytoin.t: Phenytoin There have also been reports that the metabolic elimination of phenytoin is decreased by diazepam.

opioid.t: Prescribe the lowest effective dosage; avoid or minimize concomitant use of CNS depressants and other substances associated with abuse, misuse, and addiction (e.g., opioid analgesics, stimulants); and advise patients on the proper disposal of unused drug.

Do not exceed the recommended dosing frequency; avoid or minimize concomitant use of CNS depressants and other substances associated with abuse, misuse, and addiction (e.g., opioid analgesics, stimulants); and advise patients on the proper disposal of unused drug.

bzd.t: ABUSE, MISUSE, AND ADDICTION; and DEPENDENCE AND WITHDRAWAL REACTIONS Concomitant use of benzodiazepines and opioids may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death (see WARNINGS ).
The use of benzodiazepines, including diazepam, exposes users to risks of abuse, misuse, and addiction, which can lead to overdose or death.

anticonv.t: If diazepam is to be combined with other psychotropic agents or anticonvulsant drugs, careful consideration should be given to the pharmacology of the agents to be employed, particularly with known compounds which may potentiate the action of diazepam, such as phenothiazines, narcotics, barbiturates, MAO inhibitors, and other antidepressants.

Centrally Acting Agents If Valium is to be combined with other centrally acting agents, careful consideration should be given to the pharmacology of the agents employed particularly with compounds that may potentiate or be potentiated by the action of Valium, such as phenothiazines, antipsychotics, anxiolytics/sedatives, hypnotics, anticonvulsants, narcotic analgesics, anesthetics, sedative antihistamines, narcotics, barbiturates, MAO inhibitors and other antidepressants.

cns_dep.t: 7.2 CNS Depressants and Alcohol Avoid consumption of alcohol and use caution during concomitant use of other medications that produce CNS depression with diazepam.
Alcohol Concomitant use with alcohol is not recommended due to enhancement of the sedative effect.

cyp2c19_inh.t: Prevention or Management Based on tolerability, consider reducing the dosage of diazepam during concomitant use with CYP3A4 or CYP2C19 inhibitors.
Mechanism and Clinical Effect(s) Concomitant use of CYP3A4 or CYP2C19 inhibitors with diazepam increases the exposure of diazepam and may lead to increased and prolonged sedation.

antacid.t: Antacids Diazepam peak concentrations are 30% lower when antacids are administered concurrently.
The lower peak concentrations appear due to a slower rate of absorption, with the time required to achieve peak concentrations on average 20 - 25 minutes greater in the presence of antacids.
